summary: RepoAtlas is a training-free add-on for coding agents that selects a budgeted (15-node/20-edge) task-relevant subgraph of a static repository code graph, renders it as an image plus a textual index of source locations, and refreshes the view when the agent's exploration state shifts. On SWE-bench Verified with three VLMs (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, MiMo-V2.5, Kimi-K2.5) on a mini-SWE-agent base, it reports 1.1-3.8 point resolve gains over the SeeRepo multimodal-graph baseline with slightly fewer input tokens and model calls.

claims.claim: RepoAtlas improves resolve rate by 2.4 points over the strongest multimodal graph baseline, consistently across three models.
claims.evidence: Table 2: vs SeeRepo 63.1 vs 60.8, 68.0 vs 66.9, 72.4 vs 68.6 (mean +2.4). Against the strongest baseline overall (LocAgent on Qwen/Kimi), margins are +1.6, +1.1, +3.0. 3 runs per configuration but no SD/CI in the main text; per-run results deferred to an appendix not present in the extracted text. +1.1 points on 500 instances is ~5-6 issues.

claims.claim: RepoAtlas reduces input tokens and model calls (5.8% and 7.8% on average).
claims.evidence: Table 2: e.g., Qwen 909.3K vs SeeRepo 987.3K tokens, 50.5 vs 55.0 calls; text gives within-model margins 7.9%/8.2%, 4.9%/2.3%, 4.5%/7.8%. Small but consistent; cost reductions 2.4-6.9%.

claims.claim: Each component (budget, visual and textual channels, adaptive layout, state-aware refresh) contributes.
claims.evidence: Table 3 (Qwen only): drops of 1.9-4.7 points; per-call refresh 51.0%. Single model, no variance; text channel removal (-3.9) hurts more than visual removal (-1.9), so the textual source-location index carries much of the gain.

claims.claim: Budgeted selection captures gold files better than local heuristics.
claims.evidence: Table 4 on LocBench (560 instances): FA@5 0.392 vs 0.320 for fixed k-hop; AC 0.494 vs 0.412.
§5.4 failure case sympy-17630: gold file never opened in 8 runs.

patterns.note: Budgeted, refreshed code-graph context modestly beats text-only and linearized-graph baselines on SWE-bench Verified; gains small and Python-only.
Replacing the view image on refresh instead of accumulating context lowers tokens; per-call refresh hurts badly (51.0%).
Graph built with tree-sitter; mini-SWE-agent's lexical tools remain the base.
Evaluation entirely on SWE-bench Verified and LocBench.
Reports per-instance token and API cost within each model.

methodology.sample: All 500 SWE-bench Verified instances; 560 LocBench instances for selection analysis.
methodology.baselines: mini-SWE-agent, LocAgent, SeeRepo via official implementations under matched settings; SeeRepo reproduction produced a view in only 40.5% of instances, suggesting a possibly under-triggered baseline.
methodology.models: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (self-hosted), MiMo-V2.5 and Kimi-K2.5 (APIs). No frontier closed models.
methodology.variance: Three runs per configuration; no SD/CI reported in the main text.
methodology.ablations: Six stage ablations (Qwen only) and four selector variants.
methodology.contamination_controls: None discussed; SWE-bench Verified is public and widely trained on.

standards.artifacts: No RepoAtlas code link found in the text (only links to mini-SWE-agent, tree-sitter and a HuggingFace model collection).

biases.detail: Headline +2.4 is relative to SeeRepo rather than the strongest baseline per model (LocAgent beats SeeRepo on two of three models).
3 runs but no dispersion reported; margins of 1.1-1.6 points may be within run-to-run noise.
SWE-bench Verified and LocBench are Python.
SWE-bench Verified widely contaminated; no controls.
Budgets and refresh policy tuned and evaluated on the same benchmark (sensitivity in appendix).

verdict_reason: Three models, matched baselines and a clean ablation table are above average, but gains are small, variance is not shown, the headline picks the convenient baseline, everything is Python on a contaminated benchmark, and no code is released.
applicability: Low-to-moderate. The multimodal (image) rendering is not something a Java team would adopt in a mixed-host harness, and evidence is Python-only on SWE-bench. What does transfer: a bounded, refreshed structural view (entry points, callers/callees, exact source locations) helps localization, and the textual location index matters more than the picture; a code-graph tool exposing that via MCP/CLI to every host is the portable version. The failure case is directly relevant to Spring/Java: dependencies registered at runtime (DI, reflection, config-wired beans, message listeners across the several repositories) are invisible to static graphs, so graph context must be supplemented by runtime/test signals or explicit spec-level contracts.
